extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, scientists, conservation managers, and stakeholders submitting information or comments on ESA listing/delisting actions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural criteria for evaluating petitions and making 12-month findings under the Endangered Species Act, including standards for listing, delisting, DPS determination, foreseeable future analysis, and public comment submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five listing factors (section 4(a)(1) of the Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any species is an endangered or threatened species because of any of the following five factors: (A) The present or threatened destruction, modification, or curtailment of its habitat or range; (B) Overutilization for commercial, recreational, scientific, or educational purposes; (C) Disease or predation; (D) The inadequacy of existing regulatory mechanisms; or (E) Other natural or manmade factors affecting its continued existence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factors represent broad categories of natural or human-caused actions or conditions that could affect a species' continued existence. In evaluating these actions and conditions, the Service looks for those that may have a negative effect on individuals of the species, as well as actions or conditions that may ameliorate negative effects or have positive effects. Each factor must be considered in the species' assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the best scientific and commercial data available
rubrics_metrics.description: Determinations must be made 'solely on the basis of the best scientific and commercial data available.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit sufficient information (such as scientific journal articles or other publications) to allow verification of scientific or commercial information. The Service bases findings on the best available scientific and commercial information, including published and unpublished data.

rubrics_metrics.name: 12-month finding requirement and possible outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 4(b)(3)(B) the Service must make a finding within 12 months after receiving a petition that contains substantial scientific or commercial information indicating the petitioned action may be warranted. The finding must be: (1) Not warranted; (2) warranted; or (3) warranted but precluded by pending proposals regarding other species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish notice of 12-month findings in the Federal Register. Petition evaluations may include information from recognized experts; Federal, State, and Tribal governments; academic institutions; foreign governments; private entities; and other members of the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and scope of 'threat'
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'threat' refers to actions or conditions that are known to or are reasonably likely to negatively affect individuals of a species, including direct impacts and stressors that affect individuals through alteration of habitat or required resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term may encompass either the source of the action or the action/condition itself. Mere identification of a threat does not necessarily mean the species meets the statutory definition of endangered or threatened; the Service evaluates severity, expected response, and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate threats by expected species response and cumulative effects
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining whether a species meets the definition of endangered or threatened, the Service evaluates all identified threats by considering the expected response by the species and the effects of the threats—in light of actions and conditions that will ameliorate the threats—on an individual, population, and species level, then analyzes the cumulative effect of all threats on the species as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate each threat and its expected effects on the species, then analyze cumulative effects and consider positive effects from regulatory mechanisms or conservation efforts; determine status only after conducting this cumulative analysis and describing expected effects now and in the foreseeable future.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreseeable future framework (50 CFR 424.11(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'foreseeable future' extends only as far as the Service can reasonably determine that both future threats and the species' responses to those threats are likely; 'reliable' predictions provide a reasonable degree of confidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreseeable future need not be a specific number of years; analysis uses the best scientific and commercial data available and should consider timeframes applicable to relevant threats and species' likely responses, including species-specific factors such as lifespan, reproductive rates/productivity, behaviors, and other demographic factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinct Population Segment (DPS) determination: discreteness and significance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act's definition of 'species' includes distinct population segments of vertebrate fish or wildlife; DPS determinations must satisfy the discreteness and significance elements of the Interagency Policy Regarding the Recognition of Distinct Vertebrate Population Segments (DPS Policy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess genetic, geographic, and biological distinctiveness; decide whether a portion of a species' range constitutes a DPS by applying the DPS Policy criteria and document findings in the species assessment form/SSA report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of existing regulatory mechanisms and conservation measures
rubrics_metrics.description: In evaluating threats and overall status, the Service considers existing regulatory mechanisms and conservation efforts that may ameliorate threats or have positive effects on the species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include in the analysis Federal, State, Tribal, and other conservation actions and best management practices; explicitly consider how these measures affect the expected effects of threats and species resiliency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis of Significant Portion of Range (SPR) / geographic concentration of threats
rubrics_metrics.description: When evaluating potentially significant portions of a species' range, consider whether the threats are geographically concentrated in any portion of the range at a biologically meaningful scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no concentration of threats exists at a biologically meaningful scale, that portion does not provide a basis for concluding the species is endangered or likely to become so in a significant portion of its range. Document the SPR analysis and rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources and types of information for petition evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: Petition evaluations may include information from recognized experts; Federal, State, and Tribal governments; academic institutions; foreign governments; private entities; and other members of the public, and the Service reviews the petition, its files, and other published and unpublished information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supporting information (species assessment form, species status assessment report, literature cited) should be made available (e.g., on regulations.gov) and used to support the finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment submission methods and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments may be submitted electronically via the Federal eRulemaking Portal (regulations.gov) using the docket number, or by hard copy to the address provided; electronic comments must be received by 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on the closing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide docket number (e.g., FWS-R2-ES-2022-0001) in the regulations.gov Search box to locate the document. If submitting information via regulations.gov, your entire submission—including personal identifying information—will be posted publicly. For hardcopy submissions, you may request withholding your personal identifying information but the Service cannot guarantee it will be able to do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation standard for information submitted by the public
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting information, include sufficient documentation (such as scientific journal articles or other publications) to allow the Service to verify any scientific or commercial information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adequately documented submissions facilitate incorporation into the best available data; unsupported assertions without verifiable sources are less useful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to consider taxonomy, life history, ecology, and stressors
rubrics_metrics.description: The Service's evaluations include thorough reviews of taxonomy, life history, ecology, and stressors to the species as part of species assessment forms and species status assessment reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taxonomic revisions can change the biological entities to be assessed and may require reevaluation of prior findings (as illustrated by prior withdrawals and court-ordered reevaluations). Include species-specific biological information in the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance notice and further rulemaking procedures for delisting or removal
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Service determines issuing a proposed rule to remove a species from the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife is supported by the best information available, formal rulemaking will follow with opportunity for additional review and comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This document functions as an advance notice seeking information (e.g., on taxonomy, status, habitats) to inform potential new rulemaking; public input may inform whether a proposed delisting rule is issued.
